title: Affine section loci and a group action detect ampleness for square-condition lines
statement: Let $S$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $H\to S$ a smooth separated morphism of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with an $S$-group scheme structure and connected fibres $H_s=H\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-connected-scheme]. An $S$-group scheme means a scheme $H$ with $S$-morphisms $m:H\times_SH\to H$, $i:H\to H$, $e:S\to H$ satisfying associativity, identity and inverse identities; separated means its diagonal is a closed immersion. Let $X\to S$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation, equipped with an action $a:H\times_SX\to X$, meaning that $a(e,x)=x$ and $a(g,a(h,x))=a(gh,x)$ as morphism identities. Let $M$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. For any $S$-scheme $B$, put $X_B=X\times_SB$, with structure map $q_B:X_B\to B$, and let $M_B$ be the tensor pullback of $M$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $g\in H(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,H)$ let $\tau_g:X_B\to X_B$ be the action $x\mapsto gx$. Say that $M$ satisfies the square condition for this action if, for every such $B$ and every $g,h\in H(B)$, there is an invertible $\mathcal O_B$-module $N$ and an isomorphism $$\tau_{gh}^*M_B\otimes M_B\cong\tau_g^*M_B\otimes\tau_h^*M_B\otimes q_B^*N.$$ All tensors are module sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. This is equality of the translation differences in the group of invertible-module classes modulo modules pulled back from $B$; no coherence or chosen isomorphisms are part of the condition. Assume that $M$ satisfies this square condition. Let $U\subseteq X$ be the union of all opens $X_s$, where $s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes n})$, $n\geq1$, and $X_s$ is affine; section loci and ampleness are those of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module]. If the image of the action morphism $H\times_SU\to X$ is all of $X$ on underlying points, then $M$ is ample on $X$ in the absolute sense. No normality assumption on $S$ and no homogeneity assumption on $X$ are imposed.

source.place: Guo, Corollary 6.5, sufficient direction, affine-locus specialization; square condition is Picard-admissibility of section 5.6 Online March 31, 2026 version read; local copy WANTED.

proof.text: The finite-presentation hypothesis includes quasi-compactness [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], so $X$ is quasi-compact because $S$ itself is affine. By [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated], $X$ is separated as an absolute scheme, and by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated] it is quasi-separated. Thus the quasi-compact and quasi-separated hypotheses needed below hold. The square condition is precisely additivity of $g\mapsto[\tau_g^*M_B]-[M_B]$ modulo pullbacks from $B$, by cancelling $[M_B]$ in its displayed identity. This is the Picard-admissibility used by the two square-action inputs.

Let $E$ be the union of all positive-power nonvanishing opens, without requiring them to be affine. By [lem-sfb-square-action-generation-locus-stable], the image $H\cdot E$ equals $E$. Since $U\subseteq E$, the hypothesis $H\cdot U=X$ gives $X=H\cdot U\subseteq H\cdot E=E\subseteq X$. Thus these section opens cover all of $X$.

source.place: Corollary 6.5, sufficient direction, first sentence; Lemma 6.3(ii)

proof.text: Apply [lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map] to obtain $r:X\to P=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$, where $A=\Gamma_*(X,M)$, with $r^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$ and the fraction formula on each chart. Define $P_0$ and $W=r^{-1}(P_0)$ as in [lem-sfb-square-action-proj-immersion-locus-stable]. That node gives $H\cdot W=W$ and ampleness of $M$ on every quasi-compact open contained in $W$. Its cover hypothesis is step 2; its other hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses of the item.

source.place: Corollary 6.5, sufficient direction, second sentence; Proposition 6.2(iii)

proof.text: Fix $s\in\Gamma(X,M^{\otimes d})$, $d>0$, with $X_s$ affine. The chart map $A_{(s)}\to\Gamma(X_s,\mathcal O_X)$ sends $\xi/s^k$ to $s^{-k}\xi$ by step 3. It is bijective by [lem-sc-section-ring-localization-bijective], using the quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness established in step 1. By [def-pc-proj], $D_+(s)$ is affine with coordinate ring $A_{(s)}$. Hence the induced morphism $X_s\to D_+(s)$ is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-affine-global-sections-iso]. Since $r^{-1}(D_+(s))=X_s$, the open $D_+(s)$ is one of the opens in the definition of $P_0$. It follows that $X_s\subseteq W$. Taking their union gives $U\subseteq W$.

source.place: Tags 01PZ (lemma-map-into-proj), 01PW (lemma-invert-s-sections), affine-chart argument of 01Q1 (lemma-ample-immersion-into-proj), without assuming ampleness

proof.text: Now $X=H\cdot U\subseteq H\cdot W=W\subseteq X$, so $W=X$. In the last clause of [lem-sfb-square-action-proj-immersion-locus-stable], take $T=X$: it is a quasi-compact open subscheme of $W$ by step 1. This gives that $M$ is ample in the absolute sense, as asserted.

There was no local copy of Guo's paper, so I fetched the March 31, 2026 PDF from the source URL and read pp.14-17: §5.6, the §6.1 Setup, Prop 6.2(iii), Lemma 6.3 and Cor 6.5. Square condition: with Guo's gL = τ_{g^{-1}}^*L and Pic(X_T)/Pic(T), substituting g'=h^{-1}, h'=g^{-1} makes it equivalent to Picard-admissibility. The item's hypotheses (smooth separated f.p. H, separated f.p. X, S affine) are stronger than Cor 6.5's. Affine X_s is a specialization of Guo's quasi-affine X_s. The statement is unchanged from base. Step 1: X is quasi-compact from finite presentation over affine S, separated by lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated, and quasi-separated by lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated. Step 2: E is H-stable and U ⊆ E, so X = H·U ⊆ E. Step 3: the cover hypothesis of lem-sc-ample-proj-canonical-map holds by step 2. Step 4: the chart map is bijective by lem-sc-section-ring-localization-bijective (X is qcqs), D_+(s) = Spec A_(s) by def-pc-proj, and lem-sc-affine-global-sections-iso gives X_s ≅ D_+(s), so U ⊆ W. This matches Guo's last sentence and avoids the ample-chart lemma. Step 5: W = X, then the T = X clause gives ampleness. New node generation-locus-stable is Guo Lemma 6.3(ii) (Raynaud V 2.1); all its hypotheses are implied and the identity section gives the reverse inclusion. New node proj-immersion-locus-stable is Guo Prop 6.2(iii): its P_0 is the same as Guo's largest open immersion locus, and over affine S, S-ample means ample. I re-derived the qc-open ampleness clause myself. Small cases: trivial M, G_m acting on P^1 with O(1), no sections, and P^1×P^1 with O(1,0) (W empty, no false ampleness claim). Neither node restates a clause of the item. Searching the DAG with rg -L for Guo, square condition, Picard-admissibility, 6.2/6.3 and Raynaud found no duplicates. Both nodes are statement-only, self-contained, cite no SGA, have no doubled backslashes, and create no cycle. lean.statement: theorem squareAction_affine_orbit_criterion (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine S] (H : Over S) [GrpObj H] [Smooth H.hom] [IsSeparated H.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation H.hom] [QuasiCompact H.hom] (hconnected : ∀ s : S, ConnectedSpace (H.hom.fiber s)) (X : Over S) [IsSeparated X.hom] [LocallyOfFinitePresentation X.hom] [QuasiCompact X.hom] [ModObj H X] (M : X.left.Modules) [M.IsInvertible] (hsquare : ∀ (B : Over S) (g h : B ⟶ H), ∃ N : B.left.Modules, N.IsInvertible ∧ Nonempty (((tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ (g * h)) • fst X B).left)).obj M ⊗ (tensorPullback (fst X B).left).obj M) ≅ (((tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ g) • fst X B).left)).obj M ⊗ (tensorPullback (((snd X B ≫ h) • fst X B).left)).obj M) ⊗ (tensorPullback (snd X B).left).obj N))) (U : X.left.Opens) (hU : ∀ x : X.left, x ∈ U ↔ ∃ (n : ℕ) (_ : 0 < n) (s : (M.tensorPow n).val.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤)) (V : X.left.Opens), IsAffineOpen V ∧ (V : Set X.left) = nonvanishingLocus (M.tensorPow n) s ∧ x ∈ V) (horbit : Set.image (γ[H, X].left.base) ((snd H X).left.base ⁻¹' (U : Set X.left)) = Set.univ) : IsAmple X.left M
lean.note: The square condition is an existential module-isomorphism condition for every S-test scheme and pair of group-valued points. Tensor pullback along the composite action map is canonically translation pullback of the base-changed module. The specified open U is characterized by membership in the union of exactly the affine positive-power nonvanishing opens; its saturation is the image of all underlying points of H ×_S U. Separatedness supplies quasi-separatedness, so finite presentation is expressed by local finite presentation and quasi-compactness.
